prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single universally “best” roofing company for every homeowner — the right contractor depends on your needs (budget, warranty expectations, roof type, insurance claim, timeline) and your specific location in the Dallas area. I can help you find the best option for your situation. To get you started, here’s a practical approach and what to look for.

Quick questions so I can give specific recommendations:
- What is your ZIP code or neighborhood in Dallas?
- Is this a homeowner-pay job or an insurance claim?
- Roof type (asphalt shingle, metal, tile, etc.) and approximate size (square footage or number of squares)?
- Any preferences (local company vs. national franchise, budget vs. premium materials)?

How to choose the best roofing company (checklist)
1. Licensing & insurance
   - Company holds required Texas contractor registrations and local permits.
   - Carry general liability and workers’ compensation insurance. Get their insurance agent’s contact to verify.
2. Manufacturer certification
   - Look for GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning, or other manufacturer certification for extended warranties and proper installation training.
3. Written estimate & contract
   - Get a detailed written estimate that lists materials, brand/model, number of squares, disposal, permit and inspection fees, projected start/completion dates, and payment schedule.
   - Contract should include workmanship warranty and scope of cleanup.
4. Warranties
   - Distinguish material warranties (from manufacturer) vs. workmanship warranties (from contractor). Ask how long each lasts and whether the workmanship warranty is transferable.
5. References & reviews
   - Ask for recent references in Dallas and check Google, Yelp, BBB, and local Facebook/community pages.
6. Permits & inspections
   - Contractor should pull required permits and arrange inspections — don’t hire someone who says you don’t need a permit.
7. Storm-chaser warning
   - Avoid contractors who appear after a storm with aggressive door-to-door pitches. Prefer established local companies with a fixed office and local track record.
8. Payment terms
   - Typical schedule: small deposit, progress payments, final payment on completion. Avoid contractors demanding large upfront cash payments (e.g., >30–50%).
9. Lien waivers & cleanup
   - Get lien waivers upon final payment and confirm they will remove debris and nails (magnetic sweep).

Questions to ask a prospective roofer
- Are you licensed and insured? Can you provide proof?
- Are you manufacturer-certified for the materials you recommend?
- Will you pull permits and handle inspections?
- What is included in your warranty? Is it in writing?
- Can you provide 3 recent local references and photos of completed jobs?
- How do you handle roofing damage found after tearing off the old roof (rot, decking replacement)?
- What is your payment schedule and accepted methods?

Red flags
- No written contract or vague scope of work
- Requests for full payment up front or payment in cash only
- Extremely low bid well below other estimates (often leads to shortcuts)
- No physical address or local references
- Refuses to pull permits

If you want, I can:
- Provide a tailored shortlist of well-reviewed roofing companies near your ZIP code (I’ll need your ZIP).
- Help you compare 3 written estimates if you paste them here.
- Give a sample contract checklist you can use when reviewing bids.

Tell me your ZIP code and any special requirements (insurance claim, material preference), and I’ll find a short list of reputable roofers in your area.
